normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: Remove stray spaces before Arabic question marks.

English 'you guys' and Arabic أيها الرفاق are register-specific; review whether this belongs in the target MSA learner register.
Arabic asks when the person will decide to start; English asks when they plan to start. Tighten volition/planning equivalence.
The target is a literal 'go swimming naked' formulation and omits English 'ever'; review register and learner appropriateness for standard MSA.
Requires a true causative/tailoring construction rather than a literal sewing verb; native review required before promotion.
Normalize فضلًا punctuation/orthography for polite request style.
English says 'so angry'; Arabic only says 'angry'. Add degree if exact alignment is desired.
ما رأيك asks opinion; English 'How do you feel about that now?' can be affective. Review intended sense.
Normalize conjunction spacing from 'و أقابلك' to 'وأقابلك'.
Arabic says 'the books'; English says 'those books'. Add تلك if deictic precision is required.
Arabic تريد is more direct 'want'; English 'would you like' is softer. Consider a politeness-aligned form.
في العادة means usually/as a rule, while English says often. Tighten frequency equivalence.
English adds 'Hey' absent from Arabic; either drop it or add an equivalent discourse marker.
الرز is widely used regionally; الأرز is the more standard MSA learner form. Choose and apply a consistent register policy.
